finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If 'subject' contains malicious input that is not properly sanitized, it could lead to OS command injection.
finding.assumptions: The 'subject' string is attacker-controlled and the regex pattern 're' is not hardcoded or controlled by the attacker. The 'pcre_exec' function is used to execute a regex match, but if the regex pattern is crafted to execute commands, it could lead to command injection.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: If 'subject' is extremely long, it could cause a buffer overflow when calculating its length.
finding.assumptions: The 'subject' string is attacker-controlled and there is no limit on its length. The 'strlen' function does not check for buffer boundaries, which could lead to a buffer overflow if 'subject' is too large.

finding.title: Out-of-bounds Read
finding.trigger: If 'subject' is shorter than expected, it could lead to an out-of-bounds read when 'pcre_exec' tries to access it.
finding.assumptions: The 'subject' string is attacker-controlled and its length is not validated before being passed to 'pcre_exec'. If 'subject' is shorter than expected, it could lead to an out-of-bounds read.
